standard_prerequisites: Chapter definition of normal: an algebraic extension E over F is normal when every irreducible polynomial over F with a root in E splits completely over E
Chapter lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure (delivered card L48339): F-maps of algebraic extensions extend into a chosen algebraic closure
Chapter lemma-algebraically-closed (delivered card L48337): over an algebraically closed field every polynomial splits into linear factors
Isomorphism invariance: if two subfields of the algebraic closure are F-isomorphic, an element and its image have the same minimal polynomial over F
core_obligations: Set T for the collection of all roots in the algebraic closure of the minimal polynomials of elements of E

Direction (1) implies (2): normality forces every root of every such minimal polynomial to lie in E, so T equals E; applying the same argument to the isomorphic normal copy sigma(E), whose elements have exactly the same minimal polynomials over F, gives sigma(E) = T for every sigma

Direction (2) implies (1): for beta in T, the F-isomorphism F(alpha) to F(beta) mapping alpha to beta extends by the map-into-algebraic-closure lemma to an embedding of E into the closure, so beta lies in every embedding image and sigma(E) = T for any sigma; then any P in the family splits over the closure as a product of linear factors with all roots in T, each root is sigma(alpha_i) for some alpha_i in E, and P splits completely over E
proof_roadmap: Identify the common image with the root set of the minimal-polynomial family
Extend local isomorphisms to embeddings and split the minimal polynomials
